title: PlaybookPolicy
description: The editable churn retention driver dictionary (FEAT-6, #397; part of the native distributed accelerated compute pass for UC-1 churn — #264). Maps each churn driver (a feature name, the dominant TreeSHAP driver of an at-risk account) to a deterministic recommended play, an owning role, and a save-rate prior P(save | this driver) used in the expected-retained-value priority risk x ARR x save_rate. This is the use-case skin a team customizes per their retention motions; the featurize -> train -> explain -> rank core is reused unchanged. Mirrored by zetta::ml::PlaybookPolicy in include/zetta/ml/playbook.hpp and enforced by PlaybookPolicy::from_json() in src/core/ml/playbook.cpp (the hand-written non-throwing boundary, like FeaturizeSpec / ScalingPolicy) — keep them in sync. The narrator's JSON output contract is the separate playbook_entry.schema.json.

drivers.description: The driver dictionary: feature name -> the play for an account whose dominant churn driver is that feature.

default_play.description: The fallback play for a dominant driver not present in `drivers` (the SQL COALESCE of the driver dictionary; save_rate defaults to ~0.35).

signal.description: The human-readable churn signal this driver represents (e.g. 'Repeated payment failures').

play.description: The canonical recommended retention play (e.g. 'Billing recovery / card update outreach').

owner.description: The owning role for the play.

save_rate.description: The save-rate prior P(save | this is the dominant driver), in [0, 1] — a billing/involuntary issue is cheap and high-save (~0.75); a competitive/contraction issue is hard to save (~0.30). Replaced by learned uplift once the outcome log has data.

involuntary.description: Whether this is an involuntary/billing churn driver (cheap to fix, prioritized first when drivers conflict). Optional; defaults to false.
